quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events:

options.text: Causes traffic congestion.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic congestion.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at collisions or unusual events. This is called "rubbernecking" and it causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: You see a green traffic light ahead, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Don't enter the intersection until you can drive completely across.
Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter the intersection until you can drive completely across.
questions.explanation: Even if your light is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection is illegal.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to leave the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who might cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way stop sign intersection:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver can continue without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When both drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
Speed up to protect your right-of-way.
Always stay in your current position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic must keep to the right.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Stay in the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic. If you miss your exit, go to the next one. Do not back up or make a U-turn on the interstate.

questions.question: A child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Expect the child to have full control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable and may suddenly change direction. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see, so be extra careful.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Brake hard.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition to prevent hydroplaning. If you lose control, release the gas pedal, do not brake, keep the vehicle straight, and let it slow down naturally.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Drive closer to the car ahead.
Pass carefully and do not look at the construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass carefully and do not look at the construction.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at construction or workers. This "rubbernecking" causes traffic congestion. Pass through carefully.

questions.question: A red painted curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
Passengers can be picked up or dropped off.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red painted curb.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back to the right lane when you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Increase your speed to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If the fog is very thick and you cannot see, pull off the road and wait.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing red light at an intersection?

options.text: Come to a complete stop before proceeding.
Proceed, as you have the right-of-way.
Slow down but continue through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop before proceeding.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Treat it the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road and an oncoming vehicle is coming, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at steady speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware of hazards. Staring straight ahead is dangerous. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that wet pavement can cause you to lose control. Slow down on wet roads because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: When bicycles are used on roadways, they are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.
They are easier to steer than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than cars. At 55 mph, a car stops in about 400 feet, but a truck needs about 800 feet.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you arrive at the same time as vehicles on your left and right, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until all vehicles have left before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Then proceed in the order vehicles arrive.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to improve traction.
Press the brakes hard to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving in heavy rain, your tires may float on a layer of water above the road. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. You should:

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look constantly in all directions.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look constantly in all directions.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spots or be missed easily. Always watch carefully for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park completely off the road if possible.
Stop wherever you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park completely off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, move it completely off the main road if you can.

questions.question: This sign means you are approaching a railroad crossing with no signal. You should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep the same speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At this sign, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if you see one coming. Never try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. You should:

options.text: Slow down and let others go first.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop fully, yield to other cars and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: Pass slowly.
Drive at the same speed as the other vehicle.
Pass safely and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass safely and quickly.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly to see the road clearly. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the car you passed in your mirror.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 pounds are allowed.
A steep hill is ahead.
A truck stop is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to keep control and protect your brakes.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to a police officer:

options.text: Only after a collision.
After a collision or if you are stopped for a traffic ticket.
Only if you are stopped and get a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a collision or if you are stopped for a traffic ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance when driving. You must show your insurance proof and license to a police officer after any traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel through the intersection at 55 mph.
The highest safe speed is 55 mph under good conditions.
You cannot drive slower than 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed is 55 mph under good conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the speed limit. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see you.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: In rain, snow, or fog, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your car easier to see. If you need to use windshield wipers, you must also use your low beam headlights.
